answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the incumbent refuses to renegotiate. The low-cost vendor's quote already meets the mandate, and memory_c2 documents that this same vendor delivered sharp unit-cost reduction last cycle with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, directly supporting the lowest-TCO path. The contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so the timing window for a clean switch is now. Adding a second source or negotiating terms with an unwilling incumbent would not close the mandated gap within one cycle, and deferral would push us past contract expiry onto unfavorable default terms. Running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer argues against any action that creates a transition risk on the critical path, but the archived c2 record (vendor's prior invoicing accuracy and fast onboarding) reduces that delivery-risk concern to acceptable levels. A second-source qualification with this vendor can be staged in the next review to further reduce single-source exposure without delaying the primary cost-out this cycle.
